review: The hymn follows Ephesians 1–2: 3:1–2 is Eph 2:3 (בְּנֵי־אַף / בְּנֵי עֶבְרָה) and 2:12, 3:3–4 Eph 2:4–5 with John 1:12, 4:1–4 Eph 1:4–6 and 1:11, 5:1–4 Eph 1:13–14 with John 14:3, and 6:1–4 Eph 1:6,12,14. It is a doxology, so the Hebrew keeps the epistle's own nouns where the Arabic paraphrases.

1:1–2 is the printed two-line call, with the Arabic نَهْتِفُ كُلُّنَا لَكَ ('we all cry out to You') rendered as נָרִים לְךָ קוֹל, since Hebrew cries out by lifting the voice (Judg 2:4, וַיִּשְׂאוּ הָעָם אֶת־קוֹלָם); the answer «لِيَتَبَارَكِ اسْمُكَ» is the synagogue's בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם and is kept as a jussive.

3:1 בְנֵי עֶבְרָה — the Arabic أَبْنَاءَ الْغَضَب is Eph 2:3; the Hebrew uses עֶבְרָה rather than אַף because אַף also means 'nose' and the line is short, and because עֶבְרָה is the prophetic word for overflowing wrath (Isa 9:18, 13:13).

4:3 בִּכְבוֹדוֹ נָחַלְנוּ חֵלֶק — the Arabic فِي مَجْدِهِ أَشْرَكْتَنَا is 'in His glory You made us share'; the Hebrew avoids the modern 'share' verb and uses the inheritance idiom of Eph 1:11 (נָחַלְנוּ), so the stanza's gift is an allotted portion and not a partnership.

6:3 וְכָל־עַמְּךָ אֲנָחְנוּ — the Arabic وَشَعْبُكَ جَمِيعُنَا is a verbless apposition; the Hebrew supplies אֲנָחְנוּ to make the line a clause, since a bare 'and all Your people' would read as a new address rather than as the subject of the next line.
